findings.claim: After a same-root claimant rebind, the new ACTIVE binding can use the retired binding's bearer to ack or complete its live claim instead of receiving CT_FENCE_MISMATCH; the resulting mixed-authority history is also accepted by reverse validation.
proof_refs: core.mjs:2877-2882 retires the incumbent and activates a new binding without closing existing claims.

core.mjs:2346-2352 and core.mjs:2583-2589 verify only claim_state and token_hash; neither compares claimant.binding_id/identity_digest/ctx_digest with the claim's claimant_binding_id/claimant_identity_digest/claimant_ctx_digest.
core.mjs:2362-2380 and core.mjs:2598-2618 persist the new binding as transition authority while retaining the old claim's claimant_fence_digest.
core.mjs:1260-1290 and core.mjs:1362-1390 copy claimant_authority_v1 from persisted CAS and never rederive it from the owning claim, so status accepts this contradiction.
openspec/changes/autonomous-continuation-control-tower/specs/control-tower-identity-mode/spec.md:16-19 requires old generations/tokens after same-root rebind to return CT_FENCE_MISMATCH.

findings.claim: validRollbackProof accepts a provably false rollback: receipts may claim a pre-state match while carrying a different read_back_digest, and the supplied observed boundary is never recomputed from those receipts.
proof_refs: core.mjs:1049-1052 checks only that read_back_digest has SHA-256 syntax and that read_back_matches_pre_state is boolean; it never compares the digest with effect.pre_state_digest.
core.mjs:1062-1064 trusts the boolean flags and compares two caller-supplied aggregate digests.

For an observable/compensatable effect, a receipt with a different valid SHA-256 digest, read_back_matches_pre_state=true, observed_boundary_digest=pre_start_boundary_digest, and boundary_equal=true returns true.

openspec/changes/autonomous-continuation-control-tower/specs/control-tower-completion-attestation/spec.md:43-58 requires independent read-back proving every effect equals pre-state; design.md:1315 says any read-back mismatch makes boundary_equal false.

findings.claim: The effect-manifest validator accepts negative zero for effect_index, and P5 requests accept eg=-0, despite the exact contract requiring -0 rejection; persisted JCS then aliases these values to positive zero.
proof_refs: core.mjs:787 defines safeEpoch as Number.isSafeInteger(value) && value >= 0, which accepts -0.
At core.mjs:1018, -0 !== 0 is false, so the first effect_index passes.
core.mjs:74-77 delegates number serialization to JSON.stringify, which serializes -0 as 0; scope interpolation likewise produces generation:0.
openspec/changes/autonomous-continuation-control-tower/design.md:1297 explicitly requires rejection of non-finite/-0 manifest values.

findings.claim: The advertised P5 MCP schemas do not encode the exact nested protocol shapes and limits: arbitrary objects are declared valid effect_manifest, committed_result, and revised payload values even though core rejects them.
proof_refs: mcp.mjs:204 declares effect_manifest only as {type:"object"}; it has no properties, required members, nested limits, or additionalProperties:false.
mcp.mjs:237 similarly leaves committed_result unconstrained; mcp.mjs:263 leaves revise payload unconstrained.
Consequently an MCP schema validator accepts effect_manifest:{} or committed_result:{extra:true}, while core.mjs:1009-1020 and core.mjs:1039-1042 reject them.
openspec/changes/autonomous-continuation-control-tower/design.md:1398 requires each P5 MCP schema to encode the exact fields, enums, limits, and explicit-null rejection.

findings.claim: The P5 design gives completion-race outcomes opposite to the implemented precedence and to the capability specs, leaving the normative replay contract internally contradictory.
proof_refs: design.md:1350 says a same-identity loser gets CT_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT and a distinct identity reaches CT_INVALID_TRANSITION.
core.mjs:2560-2572 returns replayed:true for the exact same identity/request, while a distinct identity sharing the committed scope fails CT_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT before state is examined.
control-tower-delivery-claim/spec.md:23-26 and control-tower-admin-authority/spec.md:45,62-65 require exact losers to replay and conflicting requests to return CT_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.
design.md:1364 itself also states that another identity naming the committed scope returns CT_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

findings.claim: The active capability spec was not reconciled with P5: it still mandates a different exact completion persistence tuple and CT_COMPLETION_* errors than the implemented and newly documented P5 protocol.
proof_refs: The spec requires completion persistence exactly as {request_identity,handoff_id,generation,token_hash,evidence_digest,attestation_id,committed_result} and lists CT_EFFECT_MANIFEST_REQUIRED/CT_COMPLETION_MISMATCH/CT_COMPLETION_ATTESTATION_REQUIRED.
core.mjs:2620-2624 persists complete_response_envelope_v1 evidence with request/request_digest/scope/CAS/result fields instead.
core.mjs:2577,2589,2592 returns CT_INVALID_TRANSITION, CT_TOKEN_MISMATCH, or CT_FENCE_MISMATCH for the corresponding completion failures.
design.md:1248-1257,1348-1350,1370-1382 defines the newer envelope and error contract, so the OpenSpec artifacts cannot all be satisfied simultaneously.
